candidate_1.modification: An aromatic hydrogen is replaced by a methyl group; higher polarity shifts clearance toward conjugation rather than oxidative bioactivation. A second change is that the aryl iodide is replaced by methyl — this strips out the heaviest, most lipophilic substituent on the molecule, and high logP is one of the most consistent correlates of hepatic injury.

A carboxamide is introduced at an open aromatic position — the added polarity reduces passive partitioning into hepatocytes, which lowers the exposure driving the risk. A second change is that the free NH is capped with a methyl — N-hydroxylation at that nitrogen is blocked, removing a route to reactive hydroxylamine species. Both changes are conservative, keeping the analogue close to the parent.

An aromatic hydrogen is replaced by a fluorine — this increases polarity and gives metabolism a benign, conjugation-friendly handle. In the same analogue the halogen substituent is removed from the ring, which helps because dehalogenation chemistry and the associated lipophilicity are both removed in one step. Both changes are conservative, keeping the analogue close to the parent.

A nitrile is introduced at an open aromatic position, and the added polarity reduces passive partitioning into hepatocytes, which lowers the exposure driving the risk. A second change is that the nitro substituent is reduced to a primary amine — aromatic nitro groups are reduced in vivo to nitroso and hydroxylamine electrophiles, so removing the nitro removes the clearest structural alert here.
